terms.comment: Lewis & Short: of every period and style. Also in answers, and after a concession “at least”: sī nōn ingenium, certē brevitātem approbā (Phaedr. 4 epil. 7).

evidence: Liv. 21.30.7: nūllās profectō terrās caelum contingere
Sen. Ep. 53.1: erat sine dubiō caelum grave sordidīs nūbibus
Liv. 22.51.4: nōn omnia nīmīrum eīdem dī dedēre
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: literally “no wonder”; often ironic, “doubtless, to be sure”.

terms.gloss: for certain (above all in certō sciō, I know for sure)
terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.12.3: quod tē molestē ferre certō sciō
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: only in the comic poets and in Cicero, most often in his letters; see sure.

phrases.latin: ‘certē,’ inquit rīdēns, ‘nam nisi tū āmīsissēs, numquam recēpissem’
phrases.english: “Certainly,” he said with a laugh, “for if you had not lost it, I would never have taken it back.”
that no land, surely, touches the sky
